item.title: Not as bad as he first seems
item.content:encoded:
As much mundanity as this skip exudes, he ought to act as a sapient Scranton Reality Anchor. ("That's impossible," the Normal Man would deadpan as the most ordinary reslity in the multiverse happened around him — a dull gray bubble of blandness in a rainbow-hued sea of mystery.) Paradoxically, the Foundation would love having this man on their side; he'd suppress any anomalous events long enough to buy them time or help capture difficult reality-benders.

item.title: Music makes you lose control - Declass attempt
item.content:encoded:
The article is well written, but I find the narrative hard to understand. I think an official declassification would be very good.

+ Attempt at D-class-if-cation
- Probably wrong in some places

The red portions of the article indicate a change from the original article. Let's look at the original text first.

Originally, two personnel talk about the technology and how SCP-3955 is recorded. By putting a music creating AI in a WARP Train from Library of Ruina box that accelerates time, SCP-3955 will be observed in the created music. A few examples are provided, and the article ends.

Except for the mysterious edits that have been placed in the article. SCP-3955 doesn't need to be contained or concealment, but its now an Apollyon class SCP. Whoever is editing this article doesn't want the anomaly to be referred as an SCP. Re-reading the article, it seems like ██████ ████ (one of the scientists behind the anomaly) is trying to stop a rogue AI (the AI being tested to make music) from changing the document.

██████ ████ has a portion of their text in the Conprocs, as there's a note that unauthorized changes are to be reverted immediately. To me, this edit in the Conprocs is very different from the other edits. Potentially, they might be losing control of the entire article in addendum 03. This addendum was made when the article was last updated, and the editor's words begin to become heavily blackboxed. Quote:

"On April 12th, at 4:02 pm, Dr. ████ followed up on a hunch regarding ███-3955's possible connections to a series of abstract, deep-space transmissions found in CRYSTAL-INE's database. Findings indicate ████ ██ ███ ██ █████ █████ ██████ ██ ████ ███ ███ ████ █████████ ██████ ███ █████ ██ █ ████ ██ █████.

There are to be no further additions to this document."

Once the AI takes control of the article, it starts heavily blackboxing everything related to the SCP Foundation. The reason for this is that the AI has gained some sentience. This is evident in addendum 04, where the AI begins to feel emotion and develops advanced thoughts. At first, it has its basic functions listed and it begins to become wary of its purpose. It starts going insane and starts questioning music, even giving names to its "cyclical" music processes. Once the AI finds the document, it tries to change it dramatically, even putting a warning in the Conprocs to stop testing. Due to its lack of access privileges, the article remains in its editing phase.

…Re-reading this, the rogue AI thin is probably all incorrect. It's just strange that edits are being made after 16:02, as addendum 04 has a log from 16:04. If this really is an Apollyon, is it talking about how music is unstoppable? Or did the AI find out that SCP-3955 is very dangerous for humans?

Probably wasted time writing that, but eh. +1

item.title: cartoon TV
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article

SCP XXX is a cathode-ray tube TV which creates a field around it. In the field, everything is acting as if it exists in a cartoon. For example, you can´t fall down as long as you don´t look down.

The other anomalous property is that everyone observing a cartoon character in the TV has their brain pattern completely overlapped by the exactly cartoon character that was observed. For example, if you look at a cartoon dinosaur who is sentient, then you will believe you are a cartoon dinosaur.

Origin story: The object was recovered after a raid on the abandoned shopping mall of ████████, what seemed like a Chaos insurgency hideout, turned out to be a place to brainwash people with the help of the TV and a cartoon of chaos insurgency soldiers , into the believe that they are chaos insurgency soldier.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Self-Casting Spell
item.content:encoded:
This is definitely a weird concept. The problem here is that you're going to have to define a magic system, at least the extreme basics of it, and then how these spells gained sentience and took on human form. Making it harder is that you've apparently decided to base it on the Catholic system, which is mostly defensive (thaumaturgy is more of a defensive art than anything else), rather than a more dynamic pagan system (which would actually be more likely for the sybiraks given when they were exiled to Syberia).

It doesn't help that spells in the SCP-U are based more on defense, such as protection and keeping SCP down.

Basically, you have what amounts to a new race that you're trying to describe, and so you need to have a pretty good hook. Figure out why people should care for it, why it matters, and go from there.

item.title: Re: LOOKING FOR GREENLIGHT/SCP Early concept: the greatest artist
item.content:encoded:
A little verbose on the history front, but I think we're getting somewhere.

+ show block
– hide block

humans always found a need to do art, of course there were different kinds of art but it was always art, so it tried to copy us thourhgt the years and believed that replicating our art is the way to comprehend what is "being human" so it currently is in this endless loop it tries to make art

This is probably as close to motivation as we can get; a desire to be human by means of expressing what it believes to be human expressions. The additional "loss of identity" aspect is a bit so-so, but it's workable. This is good!

I think the narrative of the article could revolve around the scientist breaking it's current delusional state of existence where he is so deep in the whole "Mimicing humans" thing it thinks each one of its forms are actual people with actual life historys, and after that facade is broken they could get him psychological assistance.

I really like this idea! It doesn't necessarily need to be something that the doctor means to do. Maybe they just get fed up with the mistaken identity act and they verbally lash out. You could play with that a little, too; the entity could use the doctor's outrage as it's own inspiration and couple it with realization of what it truly is.

i plan to write this all way more subtly than here ofc but that's what I have so far

Subtlety is important, yes, but you should also make sure that you don't sacrifice your core story elements by underplaying them. This is fiction. It is equally important to play up moments to engage the reader.

I'm glad to see that you've taken the time to rethink your approach to this idea. I'm not sure how much more I can do on the brainstorming side here, so it might be better to see how you've decided to execute it. Consider this a greenlight. You do need to two to use the Drafts Forums, so if that is something you'd like to pursue, I suggest reaching out to another reviewer, perhaps by utilizing our Butterfly Squad Roster.

Good luck.

item.title: Re: Looking for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Hi author!

Here's the crit
here it be

Let me start off by saying that I do see the humor in how weird the basics of this concept are. The imagery of infectious hummingbirds is compelling.

However, I don't see this concept working as is. SCP articles are typically stories disguised as descriptive files. What you have here is a fairly straightforward "Monster Manual" entry, in which you present an idea for a creature and leave it at that. While that may have been a popular approach in the earlier days of the site, I think you'll find that things have progressed somewhat.

It's important to think about the story that your anomaly can tell, moreso even than the details of your anomaly's effects. I would recommend starting with a narrative you find interesting and then building an anomaly around it instead of vice versa. While you're at it, I'd also recommend checking out some Series VI skips just to get an idea of how story-driven most modern articles are.

Have a good day!

Hi author,

I'm not the most well-read on the Tales front, but this seems to be a fine, somewhat original starting point for one. Jack Ryan meets SCP.

item.title: Re: Head of Life
item.content:encoded:
The problem is that this is a classic "thing that does a thing" but that's about it. It's sort of cool in that it evolves as he ages, but then you do nothing with it.

Something to consider is that his life could be linked to the creatures on his head; you could predict how old he would be when he dies by comparing which age the creatures are in and extrapolating (or about early 30s).

Also, a number of scientists would be interesting in studying the creatures in order to get an idea of how evolution works; they could perform experiments to see how they would affect the creatures' evolution.

The bottom line is that there no real hook; there's no real reason to care about this as you described. That needs to be worked on. Otherwise, it's just an interesting idea.

item.title: Re: Cognation
item.content:encoded:
This isn't a cliché idea, really; there's just too much going on. You have multiple ideas (The Foundation finds blood and starts using it! The blood flows towards people thinking of certain things! Scranton Reality Anchors! 3001! Ichabod project! Dr. Scranton! Old gods! 231!), but they don't fit together thematically or mechanically. Trying to put all of them together leads to a complex mess that's less than the sum of its parts.

If one of the ideas presented here was excised and fleshed out it might make for a compelling article (the Foundation stumbling on anomalous blood and trying to meddle with it is probably the most compelling, though it would take some work to make it interesting), but as-is I'm not particularly enthused.

Good luck!

Forum thread: Cognation

item.title: Re: Child of heroes
item.content:encoded:
1) Most SCPs have no idea how their abilities work; they tend to use them on an instinctive level not a cognitive one. Also, the law angle you keep bringing up is a bogus one: The standard laws can already deal with a super-powered individual, especially one like this.

2) It's actually verboten to treat The Foundation as a Home for Gifted Students. Figure out a different take on the hero, like his abilities are killing him or he's being hunted by those more powerful than he is and so needs to eliminate his abilities or has to lay low. Either way, The Foundation is not a sanctuary or somewhere to learn how to use one's ability.

3) Strictly as a side note, you would do well to switch the Central Narrative and Hook.

item.title: New SCiP: Just A Very Common Spectroscope(awaiting greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Which can turn also common light into deadly radiations and then wreck the universe

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Sci-fi

Elevator Pitch: An optical widget which can mutate the wave length of electromagnetic waves it is exposed to nearby.

Central Narrative: Beyond some experiment logs, The real escalation starts shortly after the obtaining of the object by the Foundation. As the energy carried by light will magnify with the shortening of wave length, energy coming from nowhere accumulates in the universe and finally caused… deviation of balance of material and energy. Then unexpected results, like the worst - affect the gradual cosmic expansion or bring near the final collapse.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

  • What will happen if common, visible light around you turn into UV radiation, radioactive X- or even Gamma rays that will kill you in minutes?
  • We all seem indifferent to ectoentropic anomalies now since we've already had enough of them, but few have considered what consequential, long-term impact that "generating infinite water/favorite pizzas/inks/… from void" will do to a coherent universe. But they repaid now.

Additional Notes:

  • I'm not sure a spectroscope can work as the thing. Not having any expertise in optics, so I Googled and found an effect called "frequency doubling" similar to this. But as I know all these obeys the law of energy conservation (idk the actual mechanism). What better title can be applied other than "The Spectroscope" if so?
  • Not very sure how to merge the final world-threatening narrative into this ordinary object-describing document. Will a research report (regarding the status of the universe) or a test log work well?

Sincere thanks from an unexperienced writer! This idea has been around me for quite a while. After some nearly-failed trials of longer skips I wanna switch to an easier one…


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: Unvirtual Reality
item.content:encoded:
Alright, I have given it a lot of thought and I came with these two solutions to give it more flavour and character:

1 - Adding a countdown:
While the SCP loads it could show a progress bar and have under it some strange text like "Blurring Reality Lines", "Mitigating Time-Stream Discontinuities", "Atomizing Atomic Particles", "Calibrating Dr. Bright" and one of the messages could be "Calculating next auto-simulacra event: X days."

The foundation would discover that "Calculating next auto-simulacra event" refers to the days remaining until they become a new "simulation" and end suffering a SCP breach and one of their personnel becomes controlled by an exterior force.

The only way of stopping this would be using the SCP itself, as with each simulation that they do the "Calculating next auto-simulacra event" value randomly changes.

This would force the Foundation of the baseline reality to continuously use the SCP, forcing its staff to put their alternate versions in danger. The simulations could also generate stress, nightmares and sentiment of regret in the people that play them, specially if their alternate selves died during the simulation and if they know that it isn't a simulation, but real. Amnesics are recommenced after someone uses the SCP.

2 - Adding a trap:
The SCP article could have a collapsible with a name like "Explanation and inner workings of SCP-XXXX's phenomena" and when opened it would reveal that there is no explanation nor understanding of how the SCP works, but that the mere act of opening the collapsible has informed several MTF groups of your location and that you have ousted yourself as a spy from a parallel universe, and that as long as the breach lasts you will be tortured for information.

item.title: Re: Wrong Place Wrong Time
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the feedback. I don't want to sound argumentative, but I would ike to address your points just to see if I'm on the right track to fix it or let it go.

Okay, it's been a while since I used a forum and don't know how to hide text, if any admins want to condense the following, go ahead and please tell me how.

-Actually, a third option for how he got it, Church of Maxwell does a charity fundraiser. Prosthetics are expensive, especially magical ones, and when a regular guy can't afford it, some people help him, but what price does that help come at?
-Maybe I leave out Twisted Pines, I felt I had to because of how SCP-2806 fits in, but really I just want this to fit in the Resurrection Canon, but I'm kind of getting ahead of myself either way, so maybe I should cut that from this draft.
-as far as the Lawgiver being an insurance policy, it's not that the character is not trustworthy, but I think it's a bit farfetched to assume that the Foundation knows they can trust him, so they partner him up just in case and over time he proves himself while also earning the loyalty of his partner. Remember, this is an ordinary civilian who just suddenly shows up with an anomaly and the Foundation is on the edge on whether to keep him or cut him, he doesn't just get his free pass all at once.

+ show block
– hide block

-Olympia and Black Queen, I apologize for name dropping them, I believe I will cut their names from the pitch. I actually did think out very important and relevant purposes for both of them,but since they are so big meeting someone so small, they will be introduced in subtle ways using aliases, and I kind of ruined it, but I wanted to make sure it was okay to use them at all. Olympia is not actually the original Olympia, but one of the copies that was customized for a specific purpose so while she is ridiculously perfect for that job, she is surprisingly average at everything else, so her role is to be reliably secure for one aspect of the story while still not being too overpowered and an instant answer to everything else. I like the idea behind her, but I need to use her carefully or she can go off the rails fast. She actually won't be using the name Olympia to differentiate from the original she was cloned from and won't even be fully identified until a later story, so while I know who she is, I'm going to cut the name because it's just clutter. And Black Queen is just going to make an exposition cameo which I hope will be a seed for something exciting down the road, but for now due to her nature she won't even use any name at all. The way she fits in is that she sees my character as potentially useful in her plans but needs to test him to see if he will do what she wants so she sets events in motion, but is disappointed in the results and abandons him, but not before making a huge difference. I suppose I could just use a completely different character, but I actually have an idea for something bigger later, but the question is, will we ever get to that point in the story that I need to go there now?

-Skywalker Protocol is actually my biggest obstacle. I read it as "here's all the cybernetics you could want, and the one hitch that prevents you from going Mary Sue" so the challenge is that in this interview he says enough to get the Foundation's attention and he gets spared. Admittedly, trying to explain this exception may be impressive if I can pull it off but also the biggest reason I should probably scrap this entirely if I can't pull that off. And again, perhaps I jumped the gun by mentioning Alpha-9. He won't actually be joining right away. This tale just focuses on the interview introducing the characters and leaving their fates vague, and assuming it goes well I follow it up with the next part where a security breach prevents him from going through Skywalker Protocol. Then there's a series of events in which he goes from being one of the breaches to help recontain the other SCPs, mostly because he's terrified and just does whatever he can to survive. After a series of tales resiolving the many plot threads that develop, he finally gets the offer, take the easy way out and forget this ever happened, or join Alpha-9 and he gets to keep the arm in exchange for continuing to help the Foundation.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Collapsible coding can be found in the How to Write an SCP Guide, "formatting" tab. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: The Flight of the Koalas
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Veralta. Let’s take a look at your concept.

+ LBL
- LBL

Wilpena Pound

This might not be as well known a place to people outside Australia. You might want to add a clarifier after?

Sightings of "flying serpents" are to be quickly verified and acted upon.

“acted upon” is slightly vague. Do you want to give a more specific hint so we can understand the anomaly a little better?

The Foundation History Department is mandated to research texts and information

The tense here is a little inconsistent when compared to the previous sentences. I would remove “is mandated to” and simply put “will” to keep with the clinical tone.

to collect pertinent information.

Again, being specific in the conprocs goes a long way. What kind of information should the Foundation look out for? This adds to our understanding of the scp in the long run.

during 2022

Sounds a little off. You would say “during a year”, but not a specific one. Would change to “in 2022”.

two years after severe bushland fires within the region

Missing an “occurred” after “fires”.

Compiled data indicates a severe decline in population density, upwards of nearly 2,000 per week.

Nitpick, but the second part of this sentence doesn’t link to the first. “2,000” refers to the actual number, not the population density.

It is to be noted that the surviving koala population at this point numbered approximately 62,000.

The past tense of “numbered” indicates that the Foundation is writing from a place of the future? Sorry, just wanted to clarify.

Additionally, testimonies from zoos across and outside the continent indicate that their koalas have also disappeared, despite all efforts to contain or track them.

This was slightly confusing to read. Do you just mean “internationally” or “globally”?

Uluru, Wilpena Pound, Black Mountain2, Arnhem Land, and the Grampian National Park.

Again, these might be entirely foreign terms for those not familiar with Australian Geography. You might want to add qualifiers like “near Sydney” or in “New South Wales”.

Heavy rainfall would occur in tandem

Tenses need to be more consistent, I think. You’re switching between present and future perfect tense, which muddies the viewer’s sense of time.

as SCP-5870 continuously occurs.

A little awkward. You mean to say “at the rate SCP-5870 continues to occur”?

The 2020 bushfires had burned 24 percent of the eucalyptus trees, while approximately 60,000 koalas have been recorded as casualties. 84 percent of survivors have severe burns on their paws, while 31 percent had suffered from dehydration and starvation.

I’m not sure this entire section should be under the “Description” section, as it’s additional context for the anomaly, and not about the anomaly itself. You could re-classify this section as your Discovery log.

SCP-5870-1 instances, despite numerous

“being numerous”.

share striking similaries.

“similarities”. And also, similarities to what? Each other?

bullroarers

Second occurrence of a foreign term without additional context.

These were subsequently fed by the entities to arriving SCP-5870-1 instances

This is happening quite fast, making it hard to keep track of who is who. “These” meaning the nuts? “the entities” here refer to the koalas? I would break up the description and add a little more detail for pacing.

After five minutes, they flew at high speeds

Indicate direction?

which would then hold onto them

“hold” => “cling”. Might want to also specify which parts of the snakes they hold onto.

where a large levitating island, referred to as SCP-5870-2, was discovered.

Whoa, whoa. Why wasn’t this noticed before?

It is to be noted that 40 percent of the island's surface is composed of a lake.

I would remove the “It is to be noted” as this is not something particularly noteworthy.

They then reach a small lake, wherein the main dome is located at its center.

This is confusing. Is the small lake located at the center of the dome? Or is the main dome at the center?

Some of the koala groups make their way to the smaller domes, which are not located in the the lake.

I thought they were deposited at the smaller domes first? “the” is repeated.

koalas living onto them

Unclear what you mean here.

as they are spectated by other koalas.

“as” meaning “because” they are spectated? Meaning unclear.

It is notably

“notably” -> “notable”.

dyed white and yellow.

Again, why is this noteworthy?

The koalas enter the dome.

I thought we were already inside the main dome. Best to clarify earlier where the drone footage starts, and where we’re headed.

manipulated in get fleshy materials

Sorry? Is there a typo here?

After it leaves the SCP-5870-2 duplicate at Mount Warning, SCP-5870-3 has collected approximately 5,600 more koalas.

The sentence structure here is convoluted. Meaning unclear.

the Foundation has listed koalas as critically endangered

Ah? Are we in a Broken Masquerade scenario? Why is the Foundation assuring the public?

Overall, I enjoyed this exploration log, though I felt it went on a little too long and didn’t understand the significance of certain events (like the koalas and kangeroos fighting). You might also want to clarify the description to make it clear what we’re seeing, when.

mitigated these through engineering solutions.

“these” refers to? If it’s the flooding, then the tense should be changed.

10 percent of its national budget to it

“it” refers to?

approximately 115.31 million tons

tonnes of what?

35 Small Modular Reactors14.

The footnote should come after the period.

the TIMES magazine

Do you mean “Time Magazine”?

Closely cooperating with aboriginal groups such as Bundjalung, Eora, and Gamilaaray, greenery restoration programs in New South Wales and Queensland have also been successful

The subject of the sentence is not clear – who is the one “closely cooperating”?

Foundation task forces quickly mobilize. Fortunately, most Australians were celebrating the New Year inside their homes.

I don’t see the link between both sentences?

turn over a new leaf

Personally, this is a highly cliqued phrase, though I can’t say much else if it’s officially a part of lore. Consider rephrasing to simply “turn over” or “turn themselves over” to get the same effect.

+ Overall
- Overall

1. Is the pacing and narrative good enough?

Well, yeah. It was a wild ride. I’m not familiar with Aboriginal culture (like, at all), and seeing these stories come to life was eye-opening. I just hoped to understand their significance a little more. You’ve clearly done our research and included many references to the culture and origin stories. The main issue (if it really is one in the first place) is outsiders like me don’t really see the significance of the minute events / symbols / objects.

I do like the overarching narrative though of nature taking climate change into its own hands. It’s a strong and relevant message. My major concern would be the deemphasis here on the Foundation’s role in the entire article. Basically, we’re just left as bystanders throughout the entire event, right? Which is fine if that’s what you’re going for, but removes any agency and tension from the narrative.

2. Is the worldbuilding and attention to detail decent and palatable?

Yup, as mentioned above, A good amount of detail included. Just needs to be further explained and the description clarified (who, where and when we are).

3. Does it sound too preachy?

Nope. I think the lesson is clear but not overbearing.

4. If applicable, have you noticed several problems and contradictions with Dreamtime lore and aboriginal beliefs?2

Perhaps I don’t understand the lore and beliefs in the first place. You could be more explicit in this regard, for example, providing an actual story or myth at the beginning, besides just the stone carving.

I also wasn’t clear throughout how the aboriginal community fit into the scp. There’s a passing reference to them creating posters to create awareness, but where do they fit into the story? Wouldn’t it be cool if you could show them being facilitators / active defenders of the entities as the anomalies occur. But again, I don’t want to prescribe a cultural stance for them.

Overall, I’m tending towards an up-vote. The writing is mostly clear, as are the notes and themes you seek to hit.

Thanks for sharing this with us!

item.title: The Financial Sector | Seeking Critique first
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: Tale

Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: My tale is about an accountant who monitors the budget of SCP containment procedures (especially Euclid SCPs). Euclid SCPs and Safe SCPs in this tale also have drastically reduced budgets to send more funding to Keter and other high priority SCPs (due to an incident that caused the foundation to receive a significant amount of less funding). However, when monitoring one SCP he notices large amounts of money seemingly going down the drain. After his concerns are dismissed by higher-ups, he decides to launch his own (unauthorized) investigation.

Central Narrative:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I decided on this idea for some perspective on what I
feel is like something that doesn't really get represented on the website (understandably so as it could limit containment procedures).

Additional Notes: I also would like to make this a tale series if I don't have enough space in the first tale

item.title: Re: Knock Box (Seeking Greenlighting)
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there XR Titan. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I’m mainly confused: what do a black box, pulling items out of it Doraemon-style, video games and a heart attack have to do in common? The concept sounds like a mish-mash of different ideas in order for you to make it sound as cool as possible. When looked at as a whole, however, do you not see how the concept doesn’t have a central theme, message or even effect?

Ideally, you would want to choose one or two main anomalous effects and stick with them, explain them and derive a story from them. If opening a black box causes a heart attack, for example, cool. Why? What causes this upon opening it? Could it be related to what the user finds or sees on the inside? Likewise, if the opening a black box gives you items, cool. What kind of items? Are they related to the user’s childhood memories, e.g.? You see where I’m going with this? Any effect you introduce to the concept should be thematically linked in some way.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll try my best to reply again. All the best!
